title: Talk to the supervisor from the page: the input box is the person's command, the trace reads You → supervisor, a stopped supervisor refuses it
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (the module comment's write rules, `input`, `typed`, `submit_human_input`, and how `/api/session/<id>` and `/api/fleet/<id>/commands` answer); crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql `spawn_human_input` and `spawn_submit` (the command a person's input makes, the one `spawn submit --principal human` makes); crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs `input` (an input to a session that runs no execution fails, "<session> runs no execution"); web/src/commands.ts (`commandHead`, `principalWords`), web/src/trace.ts (`deriveTrace`, `KnownCommand`), web/src/components/Timeline.tsx and trace/TraceView.tsx (how the session page builds its trace), web/src/components/fleet/InputBox.tsx and web/src/input.ts (the page's input box and how it shows a refusal); rsi/scenarios/015.sh (a person's input that waits for the turn: keep it green).

The problem. The owner talks to the supervisor through `spawn submit --principal human` in a shell (design §9 lists talking to it from the UI as not built). The page's input box posts the same command, but the page does not make it a conversation: its trace labels the person's message `You → input` (who, then the action), not who it went to, so the supervisor's page does not read as "You → supervisor" followed by its answer; and an input to a supervisor that runs nothing is taken (202) and only fails later in the Bridge, so the person learns it went nowhere only by watching the command list.

Required behaviour. (a) `POST /api/session/<id>/input` with a text and an idempotency key keeps today's guards and its command, exactly the one `spawn submit --principal human` makes (principal `human`, the session's agent, action `{"type":"input","text":…}`), typed once. (b) Refused when nothing runs: when the session runs no execution (it never ran one, or its latest has ended), the answer is 409 with a reason that says it runs no execution (as "<session> runs no execution: an input needs a running engine; resume the session"), and no command is made; a session no agent has used stays 404. `spawn submit` (the CLI and the supervisor's path) is unchanged: it records the command, which finishes failed with the Bridge's reason. (c) The trace names who a person's input went to: `commandHead(principal, action, to)` in web/src/commands.ts, given `to` (the agent's name) for an `input`, reads `<who> → <to>` (`You → supervisor`), and without `to` reads as today; `deriveTrace(events, now, executions, commands, to)` in web/src/trace.ts takes the session's agent name as a fifth argument (optional, default none) and labels each command span with `commandHead(principal, action, to)`; the session page passes `supervisor` for the supervisor's session (session_supervisor) and the agent's name or id for any other, so the supervisor's page reads `You → supervisor` and then the supervisor's answer, in the same view. The input box shows a 409's reason as its refusal. The gate loads web/src/trace.ts with node alone (type stripping, no bundler, no packages): trace.ts and everything it imports must load that way, with relative imports that name their `.ts` file, `import type` for anything used only as a type, no package imports, and only erasable TypeScript (no enum, namespace or parameter property); a trace.ts that does not load fails check (2).

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/040.sh (read its header): a real loop with the supervisor on a fake engine that answers each prompt, and `spawn serve` on a loopback port; (1) the page's input answers 202 with the command, which is the one `spawn submit --principal human` makes (as a CLI one beside it is), is typed once and answered, and the same key returns the same command; (2) the trace, as web/src/trace.ts's `deriveTrace` derives it from what the API serves with `to` = `supervisor`, has a command span labelled `You → supervisor` for each input, summarised by its text, each followed by a turn span; (3) after a person stops the supervisor, the page's input answers 409 saying it runs no execution and records no command, a CLI input is recorded and fails saying the same, and the supervisor is not started again. It fails at (2) on the live main (a484b2c7): the span reads `You → input`.

What it saves. The owner talks to the supervisor from the page it already watches, sees the exchange as a conversation, and learns at once when the supervisor is not running, instead of opening a shell, typing `spawn submit`, and reading the command list to find out whether it arrived.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
